chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Miskan, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:

Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said: A woman performs salat (prayer) in three garments: a waist-wrapper, a shift, and a khimar; and it does not harm her that she cover herself with the khimar. If she does not find that, then with two garments: she wraps herself with one of them and covers herself with the other. I said: Then if it is a shift and a wrap, and she does not have a head-covering? He said: There is no problem if she covers herself with a wrap; and if it does not suffice her, then she should wear it lengthwise.

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman, referring here to the female worshipper
key_terms.تَتَقَنَّعُ: she covers her head or veils herself
key_terms.تَتَّزِرُ: she wraps herself with a garment around the lower body
key_terms.خِمَارٍ: a head-covering used to cover the head and neck
key_terms.دِرْعٍ: a shift or long inner garment
key_terms.مِلْحَفَةٍ: an outer wrap or sheet used as covering

ai.seo_question: What clothing must a free woman wear for salat (prayer) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the minimum and preferred clothing for a free woman in salat (prayer). It explains that she may pray in three garments, and if those are unavailable, two garments may suffice so long as proper covering is achieved.
